failures.title: BMW B47D20B Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler Failure (Coolant Leak) - 2014-2019 models
items.whatHappens: The integrated EGR cooler is prone to internal cracking, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust tract or, in severe cases, into the combustion chambers. This can trigger warning lights, rapid loss of coolant, and in extreme scenarios, a potential fire risk if coolant contacts hot exhaust components.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the EGR cooler with the updated revised part is a straightforward fix. However, if coolant ingestion has caused hydrolock or severe piston and cylinder damage, a full B47D20B unit replacement is required. Read our full EGR cooler failure guide.

items.title: Timing Chain Wear (Significantly Reduced vs N47)
items.whatHappens: Unlike its notorious N47 predecessor, the B47D20B features a front-mounted timing chain that is far more accessible and robust. While stretch can still occur at very high mileages, it is no longer the catastrophic, engine-destroying flaw it once was.
items.repairVsReplace: Preventative chain and guide replacement is cost-effective if rattling is detected early. Catastrophic failure is rare, making a full B47D20B replacement due to timing chains uncommon. Read our full timing chain failure guide.

failures.goodYearsLine: The B47D20B benefits from the revised EGR cooler design introduced during its production run, and its front-mounted timing chain permanently resolves the rear-chain access nightmare of the older N47 family .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the B47D20B
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The B47D20B engine code is physically stamped on the engine block near the bell housing, but it is most reliably verified on your V5C registration document (Box P) or via a VIN decoder. Owners frequently confuse the 190hp B47D20B with the lower-output B47D20A (150-163hp) or the later emissions-updated B47D20D. Fitting the wrong revision can result in ECU mapping mismatches, incorrect turbo actuator calibration, and persistent DPF regeneration faults.

relatives.description: - The notorious predecessor that suffered from catastrophic rear-mounted timing chain failures, which the B47D20B's front-mounted design permanently resolved.
- The later emissions-updated variant that shares the same core architecture but features revised EGR and DPF calibration for stricter Euro 6 standards.
- The lower-output (150-163hp) single-turbo variant; shares the same block and EGR weaknesses but uses different turbo plumbing and ECU mapping.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement B47D20B Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used B47D20B engine only makes financial sense if it comes with documented proof that the EGR cooler has already been replaced with the updated, non-leaking component. Otherwise, you are simply inheriting a known weak point that could lead to coolant loss or hydrolock.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper B47D20B recondition addresses the core weakness of this engine: the block is stripped, and the EGR cooler is replaced with the latest revised OEM component, alongside standard seals, gaskets, and a thorough inspection of the front timing chain. This is the most sensible route for a 320d or 520d.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full B47D20B rebuild is justified for high-value host vehicles or high-mileage examples, featuring upgraded internal components, balanced rotating assemblies, and comprehensive testing to permanently eliminate any factory weaknesses.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network handles the entire B47D20B supply and fit process, including ECU coding and DPF regeneration resets, backed by a nationwide 12-month warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The B47D20B sits in highly desirable F-generation vehicles, such as the F30 320d or F48 X1, which typically retain values between £7,000 and £20,000. Because the replacement cost is well within the vehicle's retained value, a reconditioned B47D20B engine is a financially sound investment compared to parting out the vehicle.

mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW B47D20B engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned BMW B47D20B engine costs between £2,800 and £4,500 for supply only, or £3,320 to £5,280 fully fitted by an independent specialist. Used units start around £1,500 but carry inherent EGR cooler risks. Full rebuilds range from £3,800 to £5,800 supply only. Labour typically adds 8-12 hours at £65-£90/hr.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure with the B47D20B engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dominant failure is EGR cooler cracking and internal coolant leaks, typically occurring between 60,000 and 120,000 miles. The integrated EGR cooler can leak coolant into the exhaust tract or combustion chambers. Symptoms include rapid coolant loss, warning lights, and in extreme cases, a potential fire risk. If caught early, replacing the EGR cooler with the revised part is a straightforward fix.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW models use the B47D20B engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B47D20B was fitted to the BMW 120d, 220d, 320d, 420d, 520d, X1 sDrive20d/xDrive20d, and X3 xDrive20d between 2014 and 2019. It produces 190 hp (140 kW) and 400 Nm of torque. It is most commonly found in the F30 3 Series and F10 5 Series. Always verify fitment, as output tunes varied by chassis and emissions standard.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned B47D20B engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned B47D20B is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the inherent EGR cooler risks of this design. Used engines rarely come with documented proof that the EGR cooler has been replaced with the updated, non-leaking component. Reconditioned units are stripped, cleaned, and rebuilt with the latest revised EGR cooler and inspected front timing chain as standard. This eliminates the primary failure point before the engine is installed.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the B47D20B and not the B47D20A?

acceptedAnswer.text: The exact engine code is stamped on the engine block near the bell housing and is definitively listed on your V5C registration document (Box P). The B47D20B is a 190hp variant, often featuring sequential twin-turbo or specific single-turbo mapping depending on the exact chassis. The B47D20A is typically a 150-163hp single-turbo setup. Fitting the wrong revision can cause ECU mapping mismatches, incorrect turbo actuator calibration, and persistent DPF regeneration faults.
